Hi team + Ayesha,

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. As NovaMed moves to a phased warmup next month we want to make sure Redwood’s side has a clearly scoped safety net so there are no dropped requests during their initial ramp. Two asks from product/CS that we need to resolve by EOD Monday: 

1) Formal quota uplift ask: NovaMed plans a 10x spike across a 72-hour window starting 2026-05-05 with peak concurrency around 1.2k reqs/min. They are requesting a temporary rate uplift and a short-term entitlement. I’ve attached a draft traffic matrix (warmup_traffic_matrix.xlsx) and the preliminary quota-ask-form.pdf. Please review numbers for plausibility.

2) Product clarifications: Are there any sequence-length or streaming caveats we should surface to NovaMed’s engineers if we switch to the lower-latency model variant during surge? Priya — any product flags that would change expected per-token costs?

Karthik/David — can infra confirm whether we can auto-fallback to a quantized variant if capacity hits 95%? If so, we want to list that as part of the safety net.

Ayesha — if you can confirm the expected traffic distribution (percent reads vs. chat generation, avg tokens per response) we’ll finalize the ask form and route to quota-ops.

Proposed next steps (short):
- Today: internal confirmation of fallback and cost deltas (Karthik/David/Priya)
- Monday AM: finalize quota form and submit to Ops (Marissa to own submission)
- Tuesday: Ops approval or follow-up.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — want to avoid surprises on day one of warmup.

Best,

Thanks Soojin — quick answers from product-routing side: 

- Auto-fallback to a quantized compatible variant is supported, but it’s not always transparent to latency for streaming workloads. For generation-heavy traffic (avg response tokens > 200) you may see tail latency increase by ~15-30ms on the fallback model; this is usually acceptable but depends on SLOs.
- Cost delta: switching to the quantized variant reduces per-token GPU cost by ~30% in our tests for the target model family; however, if NovaMed uses function-calling we need to confirm compatibility — Priya, can you check function call behavior on quantized run-paths?
- We can gate the fallback rule at 95% absolute GPU utilization per shard and enable a staggered fallback (per-region) to avoid global drops. This requires Ops to accept a temporary routing policy change.

I’ll flag any sequence-length caveats once Priya confirms function-calling. Also note: warmup matrix shows a 40% unsuccessful retry rate assumption for first-24h — that looks high. If NovaMed can improve client retry logic (exponential backoff up to 10s, jitter) we can reduce needed headroom by ~25%.

Karthik
Director, Product (Serving & Runtime)

Quick infra constraints and numbers: 

- Current regional headroom: us-west-2 has ~18% spare capacity for the model family at baseline; with planned validation we can carve an additional temporary pool (burst) equivalent to ~4x baseline for a 72-hour window, but this requires a formal scoped entitlement and a swap window to avoid impacting other pilots.
- Fallback orchestration: we can enable per-shard fallback at 95% and add a prefix/KV cache throttle to limit replays. That will reduce burst amplification from retries but requires a routing policy change (Ops ticket).
- Timeline: if Marissa submits the completed quota-ask-form by Mon 2026-04-06 10:00 PDT, we can provision a scoped burst pool and routing rule by Thu 2026-04-09. Anything later pushes provisioning into next week.

I’m attaching a short infra checklist (referenced in the ticket) as a comment inside the quota-ask PDF. Also note that when we enable fallback there will be a small variance in response shapes (trailing whitespace and minor tokenization differences) — flag to product/CS so they can adapt post-processing.
